problem: Embodied VLM pipelines (EQA agents, memory-augmented navigation agents such as ReMEmbR and MetaMemory) answer confidently even when the visual memory cannot support the query. Prompting for abstention is brittle, CoT hurts refusal, and fine-tuning needs curated OOD categories and can learn text-only shortcuts.
motivation: In spatial navigation an unanswerable query leads the robot to an arbitrary coordinate (mean error 28.5 m for ReMEmbR, 21.7 m for MetaMemory on NaVQA), which is physically costly. Real deployments have no labelled OOD data, so a training signal for 'ungroundable' must be synthesized from answerable data.
key_idea: Synthesize unanswerable pairs from answerable ones by corrupting only the query (Q-Flip) or only the video memory (V-Flip), then train a small MLP rejection gate on frozen VLM joint embeddings.
insight: Q-Flip supplies most of the abstention signal: on SpaceReject Q-Flip alone gets F1 0.9494 versus 0.6867 for V-Flip alone, and on EQA V-Flip adds about 4 F1 points over 0 V-Flip samples. Combining both is best (0.9559). Q-Flip targeting three categories still reaches 0.89 recall on the unseen Information Unavailability category, suggesting the gate learns a structural abstention signal rather than lexical cues. Cheap V-Flip fills (mean-color 0.7136) come close to LaMa inpainting (0.7382), so removing the referent matters more than photorealism. Naive CoT collapses OOD recall from 0.95 to 0.20.
method: Q-Flip: a frozen text-only Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct rewrites the query into an ungroundable one. The coarse variant uses no taxonomy; the fine variant uses referential, false-premise and subjective rewrites. Outputs are filtered by length, Jaccard < 0.7, category regex and a manual spot check, and paired with the original video.

V-Flip: spaCy extracts the target noun phrase, Grounding-DINO localizes it in every frame, and LaMa inpaints it away. The original query is then paired with the edited video and labelled abstain. Simpler fills (dilation, graying, noise, mean-color) are ablated.

Frozen-encoder gate: the last-token embedding of frozen Qwen2.5-VL-7B on (Q,V) feeds a 3-layer MLP. Training uses class-weighted BCE on ID (y=0) and Q-Flip/V-Flip (y=1) samples; abstain if score > τ=0.5.
EQA plug-in: the VLM answers only if the gate is inactive; otherwise it returns 'I cannot answer this question'.

Navigation plug-in (C2): the gate is a fourth in-loop tool in the MetaMemory agent. It does a top-5 semantic retrieval, packs the question and caption-image pairs into one Qwen2.5-VL pass, and terminates the loop with abstention if the score exceeds τ. C1 (pre-cycle) and C3 (post-cycle) are alternatives.

SpaceReject benchmark: extends SpaceLocQA with 135 human-validated unanswerable queries (68 Object-Absent, 67 Visually-Unavailable). Train on seq 0-2, test on seq 3-5. The SpaceRejectExtra release adds 2,520 OOD queries.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (frozen encoder) + 3-layer MLP gate (trained); Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct for Q-Flip synthesis; MetaMemory agent with Qwen3-8B / Qwen2.5-32B-AWQ
setting.training_data: Synthetic: EQA uses 3,303 Q-Flip and about 198 V-Flip samples generated from the AbstainEQA HM3D train split's answerable pairs. SpaceReject uses ID queries from seq 0-2 (1:10:1 ID:Q-Flip:V-Flip, 1,618 samples). No external OOD annotations.
setting.observation: Video memory / frames plus a text query; retrieved captioned key frames for spatial localization
setting.action_space: Binary abstain/answer decision; the base agent emits (x,y) coordinates or a text answer

numbers.eval_set_note: HM3D-380 subset of AbstainEQA (190 OOD + 190 ID)
numbers.extra: main-text run; abstain is the positive class; appendix re-run gives F1 0.7382

Appendix C: 'Stacking on Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct-AWQ yields F1 = 0.7454...'

numbers_note: Not a navigation-success benchmark; metrics are abstention F1, balanced accuracy, recall and specificity, with abstain as positive. The main-text EQA F1 (0.7110) differs from the appendix re-run (0.7382) because of sampling.
results: With a frozen 7B VLM, the gate reaches F1 0.7110 on AbstainEQA HM3D-380, beating the best 32B prompting baseline (Qwen-32B-Coarse, 0.6746). On SpaceReject it reaches F1 0.9559, versus 0.8874 for the strongest prompt-based check (C2 Tool, Qwen3-8B). Naive CoT drops F1 from 0.67 to 0.31.
limitations: The fused (Q,V) embedding cannot say whether the query is ungrounded or the referent is missing, so it gives no cause-specific feedback. Referential Underspecification and Actionability Limitation stay at 0.68-0.69 recall.
V-Flip quality depends on the detector and inpainter. EQA absolute performance is moderate (F1 about 0.71-0.74, specificity 0.45-0.52), and the results are sensitive to τ and to sampling.
Evaluation uses a small subset (HM3D-380) and a benchmark the authors built themselves (SpaceReject, 135 OOD queries); no closed-loop robot or navigation-success evaluation is reported.
